title: Ops runplay & handoff catchup — May 06 2028
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact runplay-style weekly update for the SRE team: quick incident summaries, SLO telemetry highlights, outstanding runbook changes, and explicit on-call handoff items for the next 72 hours. Treat as the single source for immediate operational context and short-term action items.

High-level summary (week of 2028-05-01 -> 2028-05-07):
- Overall noise level: elevated on Wed/Thu due to a cache miss storm impacting hosted API tail latency and partial error amplification in the autoscaler path.
- SLA/SLO impact: availability SLO (region-us-west) breached for a short window — see SLO section. Token-generation latency P95 regressed ~120ms vs baseline on high-traffic windows.
- Outbound: two quick mitigations (circuit break on stale-cache backend + temporary conservative autoscale ceiling) implemented. Follow-ups assigned.

Incidents this week (short summaries):
1) Incident: cache-stampede + autoscaler thrash (2028-05-03 18:22 UTC) — Severity: Sev2
   - Symptom: sudden spike in cache miss rates for the prefix cache service (prefix-store-1), amplified request fanout to model-backend which then caused autoscaler rapid scale-up/scale-down thrash; increased request queuing and spikes in 500s on gateway.
   - Root cause (current working hypothesis): combination of malformed heartbeats from prefix-store causing TTLs to prematurely expire + a deployment of a memory-pressure GC tuning change in model-proxy that increased cold-KV eviction during a traffic spike.
   - Mitigations taken: rolled back GC tuning (model-proxy) at 18:46 UTC; enabled short-lived circuit-breaker to reject bursty cache-warmup fanout at the gateway at 19:02 UTC; increased our conservative autoscale cooldown to 90s.
   - Outcome: traffic stabilized by 19:40 UTC. Post-incident mitigation ticket created.
   - Owners: Samir (lead on mitigation), Lina (postmortem + runplay update).
   - Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-4212

2) Incident: ephemeral disk pressure on dedicated-dev pool (2028-05-05 03:10 UTC) — Severity: Sev3
   - Symptom: one node in dedicated-dev hit ephemeral-disk pressure, kube evicted non-critical pods and caused minor CI test backpressure.
   - Mitigation: cordoned node, moved workloads; node reprovisioned with larger ephemeral disk.
   - Follow-up: add disk pressure alert to dev-facing node pool (threshold: <15% free). Owner: Morgan.
   - Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-4278

SLO / telemetry highlights:
- Availability SLO (hosted-api-us-west): Target 99.95% monthly — current rolling 7d: 99.82% (regression caused by 2028-05-03 incident).
- Request latency: p50 stable, p95 increased from 210ms -> 330ms during the event window.
- Error budget: remaining budget for the month reduced from 0.28% to 0.10%. We are below our preferred safety margin; recommend pausing non-urgent risk changes for next 7 days.
- Dashboard links: see confluence runbook + dashboards above.

Runbooks and playbook changes (actioned this week):
- Cache runplay: Lina updated the prefix-cache runbook to add an explicit check for ttl-renewal heartbeats and diagnostic commands for cache-stampede class events (confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- Autoscaler: temporary cooldown increased; longer-term change PR open to make scale-down algorithm more conservative during cold-starts (PR: infra/pull/1193).
- On-call quick checks: added a concise checklist to the handoff template to run when latency >300ms (quick KV health, gateway queue depth, autoscale lookback).

On-call handoff notes (next shift: 2028-05-08 08:00 -> 2028-05-09 08:00 UTC):
- Current known issues: regression for p95 due to cache event on 2028-05-03. Watch the prefix-store health: TTL renewals metric and eviction_rate.
- Pager priorities: paging for availability >= Sev2, paging for disk pressure >= Sev3 if impacting production worker pools.
- Runbook pointers: prefix-cache runplay, gateway-circuit-breaker checklist, autoscaler cooldown change.
- Immediate checks at start of shift:
  1) Validate region-us-west availability (last12h) and confirm no ongoing degradations.
  2) Check prefix-store heartbeat freshness (>99.9% over last 10m) and cache-hit ratio for top 50 prefixes.
  3) Confirm autoscaler cooldown is set to 90s in prod (k8s config) and no conflicting HPA overrides.
- Escalation path: on-call -> Samir (SRE lead) -> Lina (Head of SRE) -> Pager duty rotation.

Action items (short):
- Lina: finish postmortem draft for 2028-05-03 event (target: 2028-05-10). Add RCA and remediation schedule. (blocked on additional logs from prefix-store team).
- Samir: finish autoscaler algorithm PR review and deploy canary to staging (PR infra/pull/1193) — target: 2028-05-12.
- Morgan: add disk-pressure alert to dev pool + run simulated disk consumption test in staging — target: 2028-05-14.
- Avery (me): coordinate runbook update roll-out and add quick-start diagnostics to the on-call mobile card.

Risks & requests:
- Request to Product: pause large capacity experiments in US-WEST for 7 days while error budget recovers. Note: non-user-impacting staging tests OK.
- Risk: if traffic increases >20% in the next two weeks (known sales campaign), our conservative autoscale could cause higher latency until we finish the new scaling PR. Consider temporary burst capacity reservation for peak windows.

Open postmortems and review status:
- JIRA-SRE-4212: postmortem draft in progress (owner: Lina).
- JIRA-SRE-4005: follow-up list from March partial outage — 3/8 items remain; see ticket for details.

Misc notes / grab-bag:
- Night ops experiment: trialing aggregated alert digests for lower-severity alerts to reduce on-call interruptions. Pilot feedback due next week.
- Training: schedule a cache runplay tabletop for on-call rotation next wed (2028-05-15). 30m slot.

Handoff checklist (copy this into Slack when handing off):
- Summary sentence of current state + any ongoing mitigations (one line).
- Top 3 alerts active right now (if any).
- Any scheduled maintenances in the next 24h.
- Action items assigned + owners.
- Link to this doc and PM/incident tickets.

Appendix (quick commands & dashboards):
- Quick KV health: k8s logs: kubectl -n prefix get pods -l app=prefix-store -o wide; curl /healthz on prefix-store; grafana: dashboard "Prefix Cache Health".
- Gateway queue check: prod-gateway/grafana -> queue depth overlay.
- Autoscaler view: k8s HPA metrics + infra autoscaler logs at s3://redwood-ops/autoscaler/logs/ (internal).

If you’re taking the next shift, add anything you see to this doc before you sign off so the next handoff can be one-sentence.

— Avery
